title: U.S. House · Connecticut's 3rd District
area: South-central Connecticut, including New Haven, Milford, and the lower Naugatuck Valley

context.text: Both the Democratic and Republican primaries for this seat were canceled after only one candidate qualified for each party's ballot line. The Cook Political Report rated this district D+8 based on 2024 presidential results.

summary.text: Rosa DeLauro is the Democratic incumbent for Connecticut's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 1990. A New Haven native who worked on Capitol Hill and as a political organizer before running, she chaired the House Appropriations Committee from 2021 to 2023 and is now its ranking member. Her official biography lists child nutrition, the Child Tax Credit, food safety and health and education funding among her priorities.

background.text: Born March 2, 1943, in New Haven, Connecticut; graduated from Lauralton Hall high school in Milford.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Marymount College and a master's degree from Columbia University; also attended the London School of Economics.

Early career: first executive director of EMILY's List, executive director of Countdown '87 (the campaign against U.S. military aid to the Nicaraguan Contras), and chief of staff to U.S. Sen. Christopher Dodd.
Also worked as a campaign manager for New Haven Mayor Frank Logue.
Elected to the U.S. House in 1990 to the open seat of retiring Rep. Bruce Morrison, who ran for governor; has represented Connecticut's 3rd District since January 1991 and is serving her 18th term.
Co-chaired the House Democratic Steering Committee from 2003 to 2021.

Chaired the House Appropriations Committee from January 2021 to January 2023, the second woman to hold that post, and has been its ranking member since January 2023; also ranking member of the Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education Appropriations Subcommittee.

Her official biography highlights her work on the Child Tax Credit (including a Young Child Tax Credit proposal), child nutrition, and a proposal for a single federal food safety agency; she co-chairs the Baby, Long Island Sound, and Food Safety caucuses.
According to her official biography, she is married to Stanley Greenberg; they have three grown children and six grandchildren.

priorities.text: Says Congress has a moral responsibility to enact universal background checks, ban assault weapons, allow research on gun violence, and hold gun manufacturers accountable.
Supports a tax code that bolsters middle-class families while asking the wealthiest Americans to pay their share, including ending tax cuts for the top earners and supporting the Buffett Rule.
Says she is determined to make health care more affordable for all Americans and is a strong supporter of the Affordable Care Act.

positions.summary: Says Congress should enact universal background checks and ban assault weapons, and supports research into gun violence as a public health issue.
positions.quote: Congress has a moral responsibility to enact universal background checks, ban assault weapons, allow research on gun violence, keep guns out of the hands of potential terrorists, and hold gun manufacturers accountable for crimes committed with their weapons.

positions.summary: Supports letting tax rates for the wealthiest 2% of Americans return to higher, Clinton-era levels and supports the 'Buffett Rule' requiring millionaires not pay a lower tax rate than others.
positions.quote: Rosa supports tax cuts for middle class families on income up to $250,000, while allowing the tax rates for the wealthiest 2% of Americans, to return to the Clinton-era rates.

positions.summary: Describes herself as a strong supporter of the Affordable Care Act and says she works to ensure strong funding for programs that improve access to affordable health care.
positions.quote: Rosa is determined to make health care more affordable for all Americans and is a strong supporter of the Affordable Care Act.

positions.summary: Supports shifting away from fossil fuels toward clean and renewable energy, and says she supported the Inflation Reduction Act's investments to reduce carbon emissions.
positions.quote: Rosa proudly supported the Inflation Reduction Act, which made historic investments to reduce the deficit, invest in domestic energy production and manufacturing, and tackle the climate crisis by reducing carbon emissions by roughly 40 percent by 2030.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, including the Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies subcommittee, in the 2025–2026 Congress.
Chaired the full House Appropriations Committee in the 2021–2022 Congress and chaired its Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies subcommittee during that period.
Served as ranking member of the House Appropriations Committee in the 2023–2024 Congress.

candidates.name: Christopher Lancia
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced after the Republican primary was canceled

summary.text: Christopher Lancia is the Republican nominee for Connecticut's 3rd Congressional District. According to his campaign website, he is a Bridgeport native and U.S. Coast Guard veteran who became a federal law enforcement officer and now works as a manager at a fiber-network company. He is endorsed by the Connecticut Republican Party and has named affordability, energy costs, veterans' services and Social Security as priorities.

background.text: According to his campaign website, born and raised in Bridgeport, Connecticut, and now lives in Milford with his two children.
Says he holds a bachelor's degree in Emergency Management from Post University and is a graduate of the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center and the Maritime Law Enforcement Training Program.
Is a U.S. Coast Guard veteran and, according to his campaign website, afterward became a federal law enforcement officer.

Works as an OSP (outside plant) manager at TNI, a provider of fiber networks to cable and communications companies; the New Haven Independent describes his longer career as being in the cable installation business.

The Waterbury Times reported that he announced his campaign on June 8, 2026, with the endorsement of the Connecticut Republican Party; he named energy costs, affordability, Social Security and veterans' dental coverage as priorities.
